bull_case: AI/data-center load, grid replacement, renewables and electrification sustain multi-year transmission investment.
bear_case: Global capacity additions can eventually create oversupply and weaker pricing.
thesis: Demand is structurally attractive and HDHE has leadership evidence through backlog, repeat utilities, utilization and UHV/localization investments.

evidence.claim: Backlog rose from ₩9.42tn at FY2025 to ₩12.31tn at H1 2026.
H1 exports were 78%; NextEra 15.9% and Saudi Electricity 5.0%.
Main plant utilization was 95.1%; U.S. transformer subsidiary 88.8%.

counterevidence: Demand is still utility/infrastructure capex sensitive.
unknowns: Global market share by voltage class.
falsifiers: Sustained backlog contraction, falling utilization and margin compression despite grid demand invalidate leadership durability.
next_checks: Update global capacity additions and order pricing.

subscores.rationale: Three primary indicators—backlog expansion, export/repeat utility demand, and near-full utilization—support durability; industry capacity response is the strongest counter.
Repeat Tier-1 utilities and UHV/local production support leadership, but HDHE does not demonstrably set global standards.
At least two material demand pools exist: utility T&D/UHV and industrial/rotating/distribution/ESS.

uncertainties.rationale: Power equipment is 68% of H1 revenue.
